1	# Training Lab (`/lab`) — full-stack plan
2	
3	> Findings verified against the live database and working tree on 2026-09-14.
4	> The Claude Design project (`f026815c…`) was **not** readable — `DesignSync`
5	> still reports no design-system authorization. Once `/design-login` has been run
6	> from a terminal, import `Training Lab.html` + the six asset files and reconcile
7	> "Build · 3 · Frontend" against them before any UI is written.
8	
9	## Context
10	
11	Fight.AI turns MMA video into structured events. The rule cascade that emits
12	strikes and fight state is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model,
13	and everything about that depends on measured accuracy — which today lives only
14	in CLI stdout (`python -m eval.cli summary | score | sanity`).
15	
16	`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` (717 lines, written 10 Sep) specs a `/lab` page
17	for this. **No `/lab` code exists** — `grep -rniE "\blab\b|training.?lab"
18	frontend/src` returns nothing.
19	
20	Since the brief was written, two commits changed the model it assumes:
21	
22	- `fc13725` added `fights.purpose` (`training_data` | `reference` | `ai_labeled`),
23	  set once at upload and never changed. A fight's pipeline never re-runs.
24	- `9bd41d1` merged `label_events` + `label_spans` into one `fight_events` table
25	  with `source` / `kind` discriminators. **The brief's Appendix cites the dropped
26	  tables and is stale.**
27	
28	The user's workflow is now: upload the bout once as `reference` and hand-label
29	it; then upload the *same source video* again, once per pipeline version, as
30	`ai_labeled`. Accuracy is a **cross-fight** comparison between two fight ids.
31	
32	## Verified state of the data (2026-09-14)
33	
34	```
35	 id |               video_path               | fps |       state       |   purpose
36	 60 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4    |  50 | labeling_complete | reference
37	 62 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4  |  50 | completed         | ai_labeled
38	```
39	
40	Both files are 612,577,927 bytes — the same video uploaded twice. Both rows
41	report 43,100 frames, 50 fps, and the same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16).
42	
43	| | fight 60 (reference) | fight 62 (pipeline run 1) |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| strike rows | **227 labels** (114 red / 113 blue) | **147 predictions** (78 / 69) |
46	| state marks | 5 (`striking` 3, `clinch` 2, **ground 0**) | **0** |
47	| rounds | 1025–10025 · 13900–22900 · 26525–35525 | **byte-identical** |
48	| `fighter_frames` | 74,083 rows, all with keypoints | **74,083**, all with keypoints |
49	| `corner_swap` spans | **14**, covering 11,429 of 27,000 round frames = **42.3%** | — |
50	| `excluded` spans | 1 (35508–35525) | — |
51	| round label spans | seeded from `rounds`, one shared microsecond `created_at`, **never adjusted** | auto-seeded (Annotate was opened on it) |
52	
53	Ground-truth class distribution on fight 60 (top): `left_hook·head` 77,
54	`jab·head` 35, `cross·head` 30, `right_hook·head` 22, `low_kick` 14,
55	`high_kick` 14, `calf_kick` 10, `middle_kick` 9, `cross·body` 4,
56	`right_uppercut` 4, `clinch_knee` 3, `left_uppercut` 3, `right_hook·body` 1,
57	`jab·body` 1. No ground-and-pound, no elbows, no takedowns — a standing fight.
58	
59	Pipeline vocabulary on fight 62: `jab_head` 25, `hook_body` 24, `low_kick` 21,
60	`jab_body` 20, `hook_head` 16, `cross_head` 15, `middle_kick` 14, `cross_body` 9,
61	`head_kick` 1, `uppercut_head` 1, `uppercut_body` 1. **No knee, no elbow, no
62	ground/clinch punch.**
63	
64	## The training set is no longer volume-limited — the brief's hero is stale
65	
66	`purpose='training_data'` across 5 fights now holds **800 labelled strikes**, not
67	the brief's 213. The 300-strike target is met at 267%. What is wrong with the set
68	is its shape:
69	
70	| Training family | Examples | Note |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| jab | 245 | |
73	| hook | 196 | |
74	| punch (ground + clinch) | 130 | 119 of them from one fight |
75	| cross | 93 | |
76	| knee | 40 | |
77	| kick | 29 | `calf_kick` 2 · `low_kick` 3 — far below any minimum |
78	| uppercut | 24 | at the brief's default minimum of 25 |
79	| **elbow** | **0** | no examples at all |
80	
81	And fight 54 (VITASOVIC vs STOSIC) holds **538 of 800 = 67%** — the brief's
82	"largest-fight share, warning above 50%" tile, live and failing.
83	
84	So the hero card should stop counting toward 300 and start showing what actually
85	blocks training: **classes below the minimum, and single-fight dominance.** Keep
86	the 300 counter as a small stat tile for history.
87	
88	## Preview of the number the page will show
89	
90	I reimplemented the scorer's contract approximately (1:1 temporal matching,
91	in-round only, minus the excluded span) over the real rows, to know what the page
92	has to render. **Approximate** — greedy-nearest instead of the Hungarian
93	assignment `score.py` uses, and my own label→family map — so the real scorer will
94	shift these a little.
95	
96	```
97	±12 f (0.24 s)   TP 84  FP 63  FN 143   P 57.1%  R 37.0%  F1 44.9%
98	±25 f (0.50 s)   TP 98  FP 49  FN 129   P 66.7%  R 43.2%  F1 52.4%
99	±50 f (1.00 s)   identical to ±25 — nothing further is within reach
100	bias −1 f (−20 ms) · jitter 2 f
101	family 54.2% (n=83) · target 61.4% (n=83) · corner read-back 75.0% (n=84)
102	```
103	
104	Two things fall out of this immediately:
105	
106	- **Timing is not the problem.** Bias −1 frame, jitter 2 frames, and F1 plateaus
107	  by ±25 f. The tolerance debate in `plan/02d-label-quality.md` is moot for this
108	  pair; the pipeline simply misses 129 of 227 strikes.
109	- **The class-count table is the finding, and no accuracy tile would show it:**
110	
111	| family · target | truth | predicted |
112	|---|---|---|
113	| hook · head | **99** | **16** |
114	| hook · body | **1** | **24** |
115	| jab · head | 35 | 25 |
116	| jab · body | **1** | **20** |
117	| cross · head | 30 | 15 |
118	| cross · body | 4 | 9 |
119	| kick · leg | 24 | 21 |
120	| kick · body | 9 | 14 |
121	| kick · head | **14** | **1** |
122	| uppercut · head | 7 | 1 |
123	| knee | 3 | **0** |
124	
125	  The target classifier is biased hard toward `body`, and head hooks — the single
126	  most common strike in the fight, 99 of 227 — are detected 16 times. That is the
127	  actionable number, and the brief's E3 ("Target zone 71.8%") would bury it.
128	
129	### The cross-fight model turns corner read-back into a real metric — and it fails
130	
131	The brief hides corner read-back behind a `Circular` badge because the labeller
132	clicks the same pipeline's overlay, so a tracker swap is copied into the label
133	and cancels out. **That reasoning does not hold across two fights.** The labels
134	were read off fight 60's overlay; the predictions carry fight 62's independent
135	`fighter_id`. Nothing cancels.
136	
137	89 of the 227 labels (39%) fall inside one of fight 60's 14 `corner_swap` spans,
138	so per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` the stored `corner` is a track
139	slot and must be resolved to a person — at read time, by flipping inside a swap
140	span — before it can be compared with fight 62's `fighter_id`:
141	
142	```
143	raw slot vs person     63/84 = 75.0%
144	swap-resolved          45/84 = 53.6%     ← chance, on a two-way choice
145	```
146	
147	Fight 62 has no swap spans marked, so its `fighter_id` carries whatever swaps its
148	own tracker made. **That makes 53.6% genuine fighter-attribution accuracy for the
149	run, and it is at chance.** It is the first time this project has been able to
150	measure that number at all, and it deserves a tile in section E rather than a
151	collapsed row with a `Circular` badge.
152	
153	Caveat: my matching is approximate, so some of the 84 pairs may be spurious;
154	treat 53.6% as "at or near chance", not as a precise figure, until the real
155	scorer runs.
156	
157	## Blockers — no honest number can be shown until these are fixed
158	
159	1. **The scorer cannot see any prediction.** `ai/eval/predictions.py:130`
160	   gates the strike branch on `_STRIKE_RE.match(row.description)`, but migration
161	   `f0a1b2c3d4e5` NULLed `description` on every non-`fight_end` point row.
162	   Verified: all 147 prediction rows on fight 62 have `description IS NULL` and
163	   `fighter_id` populated. Today `score` would report P/R/F1 = 0 — not because
164	   the pipeline is bad, but because nothing is loaded.
165	   Fix: read `action` + derive corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`
166	   (the same rule `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts:attributedCorner` already uses).
167	2. **`score.py` is single-fight.** It loads labels and predictions for one
168	   `video`. The new model needs labels from fight A and predictions from fight B.
169	3. **Nothing records which pipeline version produced a run**, and nothing links
170	   fight 62 back to fight 60. Today it is inferable only from the `_2` filename
171	   suffix and `created_at`. `ai/manifest.py` exists but is never called.
172	4. **No eval persistence and no HTTP surface.** `backend/app/api/routes/` has
173	   zero metrics endpoints; `--json` exists only on `sanity` and `score`;
174	   `corner_accuracy` and `corner-swap-recall` print only.
175	5. **Fight state is unmeasurable.** `SELECT state, count(*) FROM fight_events
176	   WHERE state IS NOT NULL` returns **zero rows across the entire database**.
177	   The pipeline has never persisted a state change.
178	6. **`eval.cli summary` reads the disk exports, not the database.** Only
179	   `ai/eval/labels/MILIDRAGOVICvsMOOSMAN.json` has ever been exported, so it
180	   reports "12 strikes … 288 more to reach the 300-strike target" against a
181	   database holding 800. Label aggregates on the page must come from
182	   `fight_events`, not from `ai/eval/labels/`.
183	
184	I ran `eval.cli sanity` on fight 62 to see what section F renders today:
185	
186	```
187	[PASS] events inside rounds            0/0 strikes fall outside every round
188	[PASS] no simultaneous mutual strikes  0 frames … (0/0 events)
189	[PASS] no duplicate events             0 exact duplicate rows
190	[FAIL] strike rate is plausible        0 in-round strikes over 9.0 min = 0.0/min
191	[PASS] no short interior rounds  ·  [PASS] round breaks are real breaks
192	[PASS] round count fits video length
193	```
194	
195	Six checks pass **on an empty set** because of blocker 1 — the fight has 147
196	predictions and the loader sees none. The two state checks don't appear at all.
197	This adds an honesty rule the brief doesn't have: **a check that passed with
198	n = 0 must render `Not evaluated`, not `Pass`.** Every check needs to carry the
199	population it ran over, the same way §3.1 requires of every metric.
200	
201	## What the page should display — changes to the brief
202	
203	Grounded in the numbers above; each replaces or re-scopes a part of the brief.
204	
205	1. **Make the run axis the spine of section E, not a footnote.** The brief's E8
206	   trend chart is the last item; under the new workflow it is the primary object.
207	   E should open with "Runs against BILANDZIC vs LUPASCU" — one row per
208	   `ai_labeled` fight, newest first, each with P/R/F1 and the delta vs the
209	   previous run. The trend line is that table plotted.
210	2. **Add a reference-pair provenance card**, asserting the two fights really are
211	   the same bout: same byte size, same `reported_frames`, same fps, same fighter
212	   ids. A mismatch is critical — every frame-indexed label would be misaligned.
213	3. **Add run-to-run determinism, independent of ground truth.** Because each run
214	   is a fresh pass over the identical video, a diff against the previous run is
215	   free and answers "did my change do anything at all?" before F1 is consulted:
216	   rounds identical (60/62 are), `fighter_frames` row count identical (74,083
217	   both), strike count 147 → next. The brief has nothing like this.
218	4. **Lead E3 with truth-vs-predicted counts per class, not accuracy tiles.** The
219	   real story here is invisible in a "target zone 71.8%" tile: the pipeline
220	   predicted `hook_body` 24× and `jab_body` 20× against 1 and 1 in ground truth.
221	   It is systematically calling body. Show the paired counts first.
222	5. **Compute "structurally impossible" from the run's own vocabulary.** The brief
223	   hardcodes elbow as `Always a miss`. Fight 62 emits no knee either, so the 3
224	   labelled `clinch_knee` are guaranteed FN. Derive this per run.
225	6. **Fight state renders `Not measured` with its reason** — "the pipeline
226	   persisted 0 state changes" — not an empty dumbbell chart.
227	7. **Corner swaps are the headline of section C, not a footnote.** 42.3% of
228	   labelled round time on fight 60 sits inside a marked swap, and 89 of its 227
229	   labels (39%) fall inside one — against the brief's illustrative `≥ 4.4%`. Per
230	   `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` this does not corrupt the
231	   label→keypoint join, but it does make per-fighter stats on this fight
232	   unreliable for 42% of it, and it is what the scorer must apply to recover a
233	   person from a slot (§4c).
234	8. **Replace round IoU with `Seeded — not verified` plus cross-run agreement.**
235	   Fight 60's round spans are byte-identical to its own `rounds` row with a
236	   shared microsecond timestamp, and 62's rounds equal 60's exactly — IoU is
237	   100% and circular twice over. The honest signal is determinism, not accuracy.
238	9. **Replace the hero: class coverage, not a 300-strike counter.** Training is at
239	   800 of 300 and the constraint has moved to shape — elbow 0, kick 29 (calf 2,
240	   low 3), uppercut 24, and one fight holding 67%. Count only
241	   `purpose='training_data'` toward training, and show reference ground truth
242	   (227 on fight 60) as a separate, smaller meter — reference labels are held out
243	   of training by definition.
244	10. **Retire the `⚠ Both` role warning.** `purpose` makes training/eval overlap
245	    structurally impossible. The live risk in the new model is a video stem
246	    uploaded under two purposes, or a run paired to the wrong reference.
247	11. **Promote fighter attribution to its own tile in E.** The cross-fight model
248	    makes it measurable for the first time, and it currently reads ~54% — at
249	    chance. It replaces the brief's collapsed `Circular` read-back row.
250	12. **Every sanity check carries the population it ran over, and `Pass` on
251	    n = 0 renders `Not evaluated`.** Six of fight 62's checks pass today on an
252	    empty set. This is a new honesty rule, and it belongs beside §3.1.
253	
254	## Build · 1 · `pipeline_runs` — the pairing and version table
255	
256	New table, **filled by hand (by me, via SQL) after each `ai_labeled` upload** —
257	nothing in the upload flow or the pipeline writes it. New Alembic migration in
258	`db/alembic/versions/` on top of head `f0a1b2c3d4e5`, with a matching ORM model
259	in `backend/app/models/pipeline_run.py`.
260	
261	```sql
262	CREATE TABLE pipeline_runs (
263	    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
264	    run_fight_id       INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES fights(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
265	    reference_fight_id INTEGER NOT NULL        REFERENCES fights(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
266	    label              VARCHAR(100),   -- display name, e.g. 'pipeline v1'
267	    git_sha            VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
268	    sha_confidence     VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'inferred',  -- recorded | inferred
269	    constants_sha256   VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
270	    ran_at             TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
271	    tolerance_frames   INTEGER,        -- set when scored
272	    scored_at          TIMESTAMP,
273	    score_report       JSONB,          -- report_io.py's provenance envelope
274	    notes              TEXT,
275	    created_at         TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
276	    CONSTRAINT ck_pipeline_runs_distinct CHECK (run_fight_id <> reference_fight_id)
277	);
278	CREATE INDEX ix_pipeline_runs_reference ON pipeline_runs (reference_fight_id, ran_at);
279	```
280	
281	Only the six identity fields are hand-entered; `tolerance_frames`, `scored_at`
282	and `score_report` are written by `eval.cli score --persist`. Keeping the report
283	as JSONB in the same row means one query serves the whole trend chart, and the
284	dashboard can refuse to plot two runs whose `tolerance_frames` or
285	`reference_fight_id` differ — the brief's §3.8 comparability rule, enforced by
286	data rather than by a note. `--json <path>` stays as-is for git-committed
287	baselines under `ai/eval/baselines/`.
288	
289	`sha_confidence` exists because today's one row genuinely is a guess:
290	
291	```sql
292	INSERT INTO pipeline_runs
293	  (run_fight_id, reference_fight_id, label, git_sha, sha_confidence,
294	   constants_sha256, ran_at, notes)
295	VALUES
296	  (62, 60, 'pipeline v1', 'fc13725', 'inferred',
297	   'b881cacfb02604e07e09b9239d5e067ec48a72d6426f964e117f9023d28fad47',
298	   '2026-09-13 08:18:16',
299	   'sha inferred from fights.created_at: fc13725 (2026-09-12 17:31) was the latest
300	    commit before the run; working-tree cleanliness unknown');
301	```
302	
303	Verified: `git show fc13725:ai/models/constants.py` hashes to `b881cacf…`, the
304	same as the working tree, so the constants hash is certain even though the sha
305	is not. The page must render an `inferred` sha differently from a recorded one.
306	
307	Follow-up worth doing separately: have `ai/pipeline.py` write these fields itself
308	at process time (`ai/manifest.py` already computes most of it and is dead code —
309	`build_manifest()` is never called). Then `sha_confidence` becomes `recorded`.
310	
311	## Build · 2 · Scoring and API
312	
313	**4a. Fix the loader first — nothing else matters until it's done.**
314	`ai/eval/predictions.py` `load_predictions()` drops every strike because it
315	matches `_STRIKE_RE` against `description`, now always NULL. Replace that branch
316	with one driven by `action` + `fighter_id`:
317	
318	- family/target from `PIPELINE_ACTION_MAP` in `ai/eval/schema.py` — verified to
319	  cover all 11 actions fight 62 emits, so no new mapping is needed;
320	- corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`, the rule
321	  `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts` `attributedCorner` already uses;
322	- keep the `description` regex only as a fallback for pre-migration rows.
323	
324	**4b. Cross-fight scoring is almost free — `score.py` already supports it.**
325	`score(labels: FightLabels, preds: Predictions, tolerance_secs, strict_fighter)`
326	(`ai/eval/score.py:342`) takes the two sides as independent objects, and
327	`build_labels(video)` (`labels_db.py:69`) and `load_predictions(video)` each
328	resolve their own fight. So the pair is literally:
329	
330	```python
331	score(build_labels("BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4"),
332	      load_predictions("BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4"))
333	```
334	
335	The only work is in `cli.py`: accept `--reference` / `--run` (fight id or video),
336	resolve them through `pipeline_runs`, and add `--persist` to write the report
337	back into that row. `Report.video` is taken from the labels side, so the report
338	needs a second field naming the run — otherwise two runs' reports look identical.
339	
340	**4c. Resolve corner to a person before comparing it.** The reference fight's
341	`corner` is a track slot; flip it inside that fight's `corner_swap` spans — at
342	read time only, never by mutating rows — then compare to the run's resolved
343	`fighter_id`. This is what turns read-back into real attribution accuracy
344	(see above). `frontend/src/utils/cornerSwap.ts` `isFrameSwapped` is the
345	equivalent rule already in the frontend.
346	
347	**4d. Guard rails before any number is emitted.** Assert the pair really is one
348	bout: same `fps`, same `reported_frames`, same red/blue fighter ids, reference
349	has `labeled_at IS NOT NULL`, run has `purpose='ai_labeled'`. `score()` today
350	only *prints a warning* on an fps mismatch and carries on — across two uploads
351	that must become a refusal, because every frame index would be silently wrong.
352	Return an explicit *unmeasurable* result — never zeros — when a sub-metric has no
353	population: fight state today (0 `state` rows anywhere), and any sanity check
354	that ran on n = 0.
355	
356	**4e. API.** New `eval_router` registered in `backend/app/main.py` with
357	`prefix="/eval"`, following `backend/app/api/routes/fights.py` conventions
358	(module-level `router`, `response_model`, Pydantic schemas beside the ORM model).
359	Live SQL for anything derived from `fight_events` / `fights` / `rounds`; the
360	stored `score_report` for accuracy. Sketch:
361	
362	| Route | Serves |
363	|---|---|
364	| `GET /eval/labels/summary` | A · hero + tiles: per-family counts split by `purpose`, largest-fight share, activity by day |
365	| `GET /eval/labels/events` | B1/B2/B3 · counts by action × target × corner × state, filterable by fight and purpose |
366	| `GET /eval/fights` | C + D · ledger rows, span/coverage counts, open spans, seeded-vs-adjusted rounds, video-on-disk |
367	| `GET /eval/fights/{id}/coverage` | C4 · the coverage strip's lanes for one fight |
368	| `GET /eval/runs` | E · `pipeline_runs` joined to both fights, newest first |
369	| `GET /eval/runs/{id}/score` | E1–E9 · the stored `score_report` |
370	| `GET /eval/runs/{id}/sanity` | F1 · sanity report, each check carrying its population |
371	| `GET /eval/runs/{id}/corner` | F2 · corner accuracy — needs `--json` added to `ai/eval/corner_accuracy.py`, which prints only today |
372	
373	**4f. Ordering.** 4a → 4c → 4b → insert the fight-62 row → 4d → persist a score
374	→ API → page. The first three steps alone turn today's F1 of 0 into ~45%.
375	
376	## Build · 3 · Frontend — the `/lab` page
377	
378	Conventions to follow (all verified): React 19 + TS + Vite, `react-router-dom`,
379	plain `fetch` with root-relative paths, **no chart library and no CSS framework**
380	— every visual is hand-written inline SVG plus inline `style={{}}` referencing
381	`var(--token)` from `frontend/src/index.css`.
382	
383	### Wiring
384	
385	- `frontend/src/App.tsx` — one `<Route path="/lab" element={<Lab />} />`.
386	- `frontend/src/components/Header.tsx:6` — add `{ label: 'Lab', to: '/lab' }` to
387	  `NAV_LINKS`.
388	- `frontend/vite.config.ts` — add an `/eval` proxy entry. **Put the API under
389	  `/eval/...`, not `/lab`**, so the client route and the API path never collide
390	  and the `Accept: text/html` bypass the `/fights` entry needs isn't repeated.
391	- New files: `frontend/src/pages/Lab.tsx` + `frontend/src/components/lab/*.tsx` +
392	  `frontend/src/hooks/useLab*.ts`, matching the existing one-folder-per-page rule.
393	
394	### Tokens to add to `index.css`
395	
396	None of these exist yet. Values come from the brief §14, which were checked with
397	the dataviz palette validator against the card surface including CVD simulation
398	(see `frontend-palette-collisions`):
399	
400	```css
401	--status-good: #0ca30c;  --status-warning: #fab219;  --status-critical: #ef4444;
402	--status-unverified: #94a3b8;  --status-unmeasured: #64748b;
403	--state-striking: #0099b0;  --state-clinch: #e64a19;  --state-ground: #9085e9;
404	```
405	
406	Do **not** reuse `AnnotationTimeline.tsx`'s STATE colours — its CLINCH `#ff7043`
407	and GROUND `#ff4d4d` are ΔE 6.6 apart and GROUND is the red corner.
408	
409	### Reuse, don't rebuild
410	
411	| Need | Reuse |
412	|---|---|
413	| B1 palette rows | `components/annotate/taxonomy.ts` `TOOL_GROUPS` — B1 is that list joined with counts; never hardcode the actions (the palette has `submission_attempt`, the brief says `submission`) |
414	| R\|B split, corner attribution | `utils/liveStats.ts` `attributedCorner` |
415	| B3 stacked bars | `components/player/SegBar.tsx` |
416	| E8 trend line | model on `components/player/PaceChart.tsx` (hand-rolled SVG, fixed `viewBox`, manual scale fns) |
417	| Stat tiles | `components/player/MiniStat.tsx`, `.inner-tile` |
418	| Card header + pills + view toggle | `components/annotate/AnnotationPanel.tsx` (incl. its `localStorage` view persistence) |
419	| Dense clickable rows | `components/player/LiveFeed.tsx` row anatomy |
420	| C4 coverage strip | **extract a shared mini-strip from `components/annotate/AnnotationTimeline.tsx`** — it already draws rounds / state / swap / excluded lanes and owns `SPAN_COLOR`; this is the highest-value refactor in the whole job |
421	| Purpose chips | `components/FightPurposeBadge.tsx`, `types/Fight.ts` `PURPOSE_COLORS` |
422	
423	New primitives that genuinely don't exist: a sortable table with a sticky header
424	and expandable rows (there is **no `<table>` anywhere in the codebase**), a
425	heatmap cell, a dumbbell row, a dot strip, a column chart, and a `StatusBadge`
426	rendering all five states as **icon + text** (never colour alone).
427	
428	### Prerequisite on two existing pages
429	
430	`?frame=N` deep links are required by C4, E9 and G2. `grep -rn "useSearchParams"
431	src/` returns nothing — neither `pages/Player.tsx` nor `pages/Annotate.tsx` reads

437	2. **The scorer, first and on its own** — before any UI:
438	   `cd ai && ../.venv/bin/python -m eval.cli score --reference 60 --run 62 --json /tmp/r.json`
439	   must report a non-zero F1 near the ±12 f preview above (TP 84 / FP 63 / FN 143,
440	   F1 ≈ 45%). If it reports 0, blocker 1 is not fixed.
441	3. `eval.cli sanity fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4` must stop saying
442	   "0 in-round strikes" and must mark n = 0 checks `Not evaluated`.
443	4. Insert the fight-62 run row by hand (the agreed manual step) — see Build · 1 — then
444	   `curl localhost:8000/eval/runs` and confirm it lists exactly that run with

446	   is unchanged between `fc13725` and the working tree, so this hash is right).
447	5. Open `/lab`. Check against the numbers in this plan: 800 training strikes,

449	   fight state `Not measured`, rounds `Seeded — not verified`.
450	6. Click a miss in E9 → lands on `/fights/60/annotate?frame=N` at that frame.

# Training Lab (`/lab`) — full-stack plan

> Findings verified against the live database and working tree on 2026-09-14.
> The Claude Design project (`f026815c…`) was **not** readable — `DesignSync`
> still reports no design-system authorization. Once `/design-login` has been run
> from a terminal, import `Training Lab.html` + the six asset files and reconcile
> "Build · 3 · Frontend" against them before any UI is written.

## Context

Fight.AI turns MMA video into structured events. The rule cascade that emits
strikes and fight state is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model,
and everything about that depends on measured accuracy — which today lives only
in CLI stdout (`python -m eval.cli summary | score | sanity`).

`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` (717 lines, written 10 Sep) specs a `/lab` page
for this. **No `/lab` code exists** — `grep -rniE "\blab\b|training.?lab"
frontend/src` returns nothing.

Since the brief was written, two commits changed the model it assumes:

- `fc13725` added `fights.purpose` (`training_data` | `reference` | `ai_labeled`),
  set once at upload and never changed. A fight's pipeline never re-runs.
- `9bd41d1` merged `label_events` + `label_spans` into one `fight_events` table
  with `source` / `kind` discriminators. **The brief's Appendix cites the dropped
  tables and is stale.**

The user's workflow is now: upload the bout once as `reference` and hand-label
it; then upload the *same source video* again, once per pipeline version, as
`ai_labeled`. Accuracy is a **cross-fight** comparison between two fight ids.

## Verified state of the data (2026-09-14)

```
 id |               video_path               | fps |       state       |   purpose
 60 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4    |  50 | labeling_complete | reference
 62 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4  |  50 | completed         | ai_labeled
```

Both files are 612,577,927 bytes — the same video uploaded twice. Both rows
report 43,100 frames, 50 fps, and the same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16).

| | fight 60 (reference) | fight 62 (pipeline run 1) |
|---|---|---|
| strike rows | **227 labels** (114 red / 113 blue) | **147 predictions** (78 / 69) |
| state marks | 5 (`striking` 3, `clinch` 2, **ground 0**) | **0** |
| rounds | 1025–10025 · 13900–22900 · 26525–35525 | **byte-identical** |
| `fighter_frames` | 74,083 rows, all with keypoints | **74,083**, all with keypoints |
| `corner_swap` spans | **14**, covering 11,429 of 27,000 round frames = **42.3%** | — |
| `excluded` spans | 1 (35508–35525) | — |
| round label spans | seeded from `rounds`, one shared microsecond `created_at`, **never adjusted** | auto-seeded (Annotate was opened on it) |

Ground-truth class distribution on fight 60 (top): `left_hook·head` 77,
`jab·head` 35, `cross·head` 30, `right_hook·head` 22, `low_kick` 14,
`high_kick` 14, `calf_kick` 10, `middle_kick` 9, `cross·body` 4,
`right_uppercut` 4, `clinch_knee` 3, `left_uppercut` 3, `right_hook·body` 1,
`jab·body` 1. No ground-and-pound, no elbows, no takedowns — a standing fight.

Pipeline vocabulary on fight 62: `jab_head` 25, `hook_body` 24, `low_kick` 21,
`jab_body` 20, `hook_head` 16, `cross_head` 15, `middle_kick` 14, `cross_body` 9,
`head_kick` 1, `uppercut_head` 1, `uppercut_body` 1. **No knee, no elbow, no
ground/clinch punch.**

## The training set is no longer volume-limited — the brief's hero is stale

`purpose='training_data'` across 5 fights now holds **800 labelled strikes**, not
the brief's 213. The 300-strike target is met at 267%. What is wrong with the set
is its shape:

| Training family | Examples | Note |
|---|---|---|
| jab | 245 | |
| hook | 196 | |
| punch (ground + clinch) | 130 | 119 of them from one fight |
| cross | 93 | |
| knee | 40 | |
| kick | 29 | `calf_kick` 2 · `low_kick` 3 — far below any minimum |
| uppercut | 24 | at the brief's default minimum of 25 |
| **elbow** | **0** | no examples at all |

And fight 54 (VITASOVIC vs STOSIC) holds **538 of 800 = 67%** — the brief's
"largest-fight share, warning above 50%" tile, live and failing.

So the hero card should stop counting toward 300 and start showing what actually
blocks training: **classes below the minimum, and single-fight dominance.** Keep
the 300 counter as a small stat tile for history.

## Preview of the number the page will show

I reimplemented the scorer's contract approximately (1:1 temporal matching,
in-round only, minus the excluded span) over the real rows, to know what the page
has to render. **Approximate** — greedy-nearest instead of the Hungarian
assignment `score.py` uses, and my own label→family map — so the real scorer will
shift these a little.

```
±12 f (0.24 s)   TP 84  FP 63  FN 143   P 57.1%  R 37.0%  F1 44.9%
±25 f (0.50 s)   TP 98  FP 49  FN 129   P 66.7%  R 43.2%  F1 52.4%
±50 f (1.00 s)   identical to ±25 — nothing further is within reach
bias −1 f (−20 ms) · jitter 2 f
family 54.2% (n=83) · target 61.4% (n=83) · corner read-back 75.0% (n=84)
```

Two things fall out of this immediately:

- **Timing is not the problem.** Bias −1 frame, jitter 2 frames, and F1 plateaus
  by ±25 f. The tolerance debate in `plan/02d-label-quality.md` is moot for this
  pair; the pipeline simply misses 129 of 227 strikes.
- **The class-count table is the finding, and no accuracy tile would show it:**

| family · target | truth | predicted |
|---|---|---|
| hook · head | **99** | **16** |
| hook · body | **1** | **24** |
| jab · head | 35 | 25 |
| jab · body | **1** | **20** |
| cross · head | 30 | 15 |
| cross · body | 4 | 9 |
| kick · leg | 24 | 21 |
| kick · body | 9 | 14 |
| kick · head | **14** | **1** |
| uppercut · head | 7 | 1 |
| knee | 3 | **0** |

  The target classifier is biased hard toward `body`, and head hooks — the single
  most common strike in the fight, 99 of 227 — are detected 16 times. That is the
  actionable number, and the brief's E3 ("Target zone 71.8%") would bury it.

### The cross-fight model turns corner read-back into a real metric — and it fails

The brief hides corner read-back behind a `Circular` badge because the labeller
clicks the same pipeline's overlay, so a tracker swap is copied into the label
and cancels out. **That reasoning does not hold across two fights.** The labels
were read off fight 60's overlay; the predictions carry fight 62's independent
`fighter_id`. Nothing cancels.

89 of the 227 labels (39%) fall inside one of fight 60's 14 `corner_swap` spans,
so per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` the stored `corner` is a track
slot and must be resolved to a person — at read time, by flipping inside a swap
span — before it can be compared with fight 62's `fighter_id`:

```
raw slot vs person     63/84 = 75.0%
swap-resolved          45/84 = 53.6%     ← chance, on a two-way choice
```

Fight 62 has no swap spans marked, so its `fighter_id` carries whatever swaps its
own tracker made. **That makes 53.6% genuine fighter-attribution accuracy for the
run, and it is at chance.** It is the first time this project has been able to
measure that number at all, and it deserves a tile in section E rather than a
collapsed row with a `Circular` badge.

Caveat: my matching is approximate, so some of the 84 pairs may be spurious;
treat 53.6% as "at or near chance", not as a precise figure, until the real
scorer runs.

## Blockers — no honest number can be shown until these are fixed

1. **The scorer cannot see any prediction.** `ai/eval/predictions.py:130`
   gates the strike branch on `_STRIKE_RE.match(row.description)`, but migration
   `f0a1b2c3d4e5` NULLed `description` on every non-`fight_end` point row.
   Verified: all 147 prediction rows on fight 62 have `description IS NULL` and
   `fighter_id` populated. Today `score` would report P/R/F1 = 0 — not because
   the pipeline is bad, but because nothing is loaded.
   Fix: read `action` + derive corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`
   (the same rule `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts:attributedCorner` already uses).
2. **`score.py` is single-fight.** It loads labels and predictions for one
   `video`. The new model needs labels from fight A and predictions from fight B.
3. **Nothing records which pipeline version produced a run**, and nothing links
   fight 62 back to fight 60. Today it is inferable only from the `_2` filename
   suffix and `created_at`. `ai/manifest.py` exists but is never called.
4. **No eval persistence and no HTTP surface.** `backend/app/api/routes/` has
   zero metrics endpoints; `--json` exists only on `sanity` and `score`;
   `corner_accuracy` and `corner-swap-recall` print only.
5. **Fight state is unmeasurable.** `SELECT state, count(*) FROM fight_events
   WHERE state IS NOT NULL` returns **zero rows across the entire database**.
   The pipeline has never persisted a state change.
6. **`eval.cli summary` reads the disk exports, not the database.** Only
   `ai/eval/labels/MILIDRAGOVICvsMOOSMAN.json` has ever been exported, so it
   reports "12 strikes … 288 more to reach the 300-strike target" against a
   database holding 800. Label aggregates on the page must come from
   `fight_events`, not from `ai/eval/labels/`.

I ran `eval.cli sanity` on fight 62 to see what section F renders today:

```
[PASS] events inside rounds            0/0 strikes fall outside every round
[PASS] no simultaneous mutual strikes  0 frames … (0/0 events)
[PASS] no duplicate events             0 exact duplicate rows
[FAIL] strike rate is plausible        0 in-round strikes over 9.0 min = 0.0/min
[PASS] no short interior rounds  ·  [PASS] round breaks are real breaks
[PASS] round count fits video length
```

Six checks pass **on an empty set** because of blocker 1 — the fight has 147
predictions and the loader sees none. The two state checks don't appear at all.
This adds an honesty rule the brief doesn't have: **a check that passed with
n = 0 must render `Not evaluated`, not `Pass`.** Every check needs to carry the
population it ran over, the same way §3.1 requires of every metric.

## What the page should display — changes to the brief

Grounded in the numbers above; each replaces or re-scopes a part of the brief.

1. **Make the run axis the spine of section E, not a footnote.** The brief's E8
   trend chart is the last item; under the new workflow it is the primary object.
   E should open with "Runs against BILANDZIC vs LUPASCU" — one row per
   `ai_labeled` fight, newest first, each with P/R/F1 and the delta vs the
   previous run. The trend line is that table plotted.
2. **Add a reference-pair provenance card**, asserting the two fights really are
   the same bout: same byte size, same `reported_frames`, same fps, same fighter
   ids. A mismatch is critical — every frame-indexed label would be misaligned.
3. **Add run-to-run determinism, independent of ground truth.** Because each run
   is a fresh pass over the identical video, a diff against the previous run is
   free and answers "did my change do anything at all?" before F1 is consulted:
   rounds identical (60/62 are), `fighter_frames` row count identical (74,083
   both), strike count 147 → next. The brief has nothing like this.
4. **Lead E3 with truth-vs-predicted counts per class, not accuracy tiles.** The
   real story here is invisible in a "target zone 71.8%" tile: the pipeline
   predicted `hook_body` 24× and `jab_body` 20× against 1 and 1 in ground truth.
   It is systematically calling body. Show the paired counts first.
5. **Compute "structurally impossible" from the run's own vocabulary.** The brief
   hardcodes elbow as `Always a miss`. Fight 62 emits no knee either, so the 3
   labelled `clinch_knee` are guaranteed FN. Derive this per run.
6. **Fight state renders `Not measured` with its reason** — "the pipeline
   persisted 0 state changes" — not an empty dumbbell chart.
7. **Corner swaps are the headline of section C, not a footnote.** 42.3% of
   labelled round time on fight 60 sits inside a marked swap, and 89 of its 227
   labels (39%) fall inside one — against the brief's illustrative `≥ 4.4%`. Per
   `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` this does not corrupt the
   label→keypoint join, but it does make per-fighter stats on this fight
   unreliable for 42% of it, and it is what the scorer must apply to recover a
   person from a slot (§4c).
8. **Replace round IoU with `Seeded — not verified` plus cross-run agreement.**
   Fight 60's round spans are byte-identical to its own `rounds` row with a
   shared microsecond timestamp, and 62's rounds equal 60's exactly — IoU is
   100% and circular twice over. The honest signal is determinism, not accuracy.
9. **Replace the hero: class coverage, not a 300-strike counter.** Training is at
   800 of 300 and the constraint has moved to shape — elbow 0, kick 29 (calf 2,
   low 3), uppercut 24, and one fight holding 67%. Count only
   `purpose='training_data'` toward training, and show reference ground truth
   (227 on fight 60) as a separate, smaller meter — reference labels are held out
   of training by definition.
10. **Retire the `⚠ Both` role warning.** `purpose` makes training/eval overlap
    structurally impossible. The live risk in the new model is a video stem
    uploaded under two purposes, or a run paired to the wrong reference.
11. **Promote fighter attribution to its own tile in E.** The cross-fight model
    makes it measurable for the first time, and it currently reads ~54% — at
    chance. It replaces the brief's collapsed `Circular` read-back row.
12. **Every sanity check carries the population it ran over, and `Pass` on
    n = 0 renders `Not evaluated`.** Six of fight 62's checks pass today on an
    empty set. This is a new honesty rule, and it belongs beside §3.1.

## Build · 1 · `pipeline_runs` — the pairing and version table

New table, **filled by hand (by me, via SQL) after each `ai_labeled` upload** —
nothing in the upload flow or the pipeline writes it. New Alembic migration in
`db/alembic/versions/` on top of head `f0a1b2c3d4e5`, with a matching ORM model
in `backend/app/models/pipeline_run.py`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE pipeline_runs (
    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    run_fight_id       INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES fights(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    reference_fight_id INTEGER NOT NULL        REFERENCES fights(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    label              VARCHAR(100),   -- display name, e.g. 'pipeline v1'
    git_sha            VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    sha_confidence     VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'inferred',  -- recorded | inferred
    constants_sha256   VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    ran_at             TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    tolerance_frames   INTEGER,        -- set when scored
    scored_at          TIMESTAMP,
    score_report       JSONB,          -- report_io.py's provenance envelope
    notes              TEXT,
    created_at         TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT ck_pipeline_runs_distinct CHECK (run_fight_id <> reference_fight_id)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_pipeline_runs_reference ON pipeline_runs (reference_fight_id, ran_at);
```

Only the six identity fields are hand-entered; `tolerance_frames`, `scored_at`
and `score_report` are written by `eval.cli score --persist`. Keeping the report
as JSONB in the same row means one query serves the whole trend chart, and the
dashboard can refuse to plot two runs whose `tolerance_frames` or
`reference_fight_id` differ — the brief's §3.8 comparability rule, enforced by
data rather than by a note. `--json <path>` stays as-is for git-committed
baselines under `ai/eval/baselines/`.

`sha_confidence` exists because today's one row genuinely is a guess:

```sql
INSERT INTO pipeline_runs
  (run_fight_id, reference_fight_id, label, git_sha, sha_confidence,
   constants_sha256, ran_at, notes)
VALUES
  (62, 60, 'pipeline v1', 'fc13725', 'inferred',
   'b881cacfb02604e07e09b9239d5e067ec48a72d6426f964e117f9023d28fad47',
   '2026-09-13 08:18:16',
   'sha inferred from fights.created_at: fc13725 (2026-09-12 17:31) was the latest
    commit before the run; working-tree cleanliness unknown');
```

Verified: `git show fc13725:ai/models/constants.py` hashes to `b881cacf…`, the
same as the working tree, so the constants hash is certain even though the sha
is not. The page must render an `inferred` sha differently from a recorded one.

Follow-up worth doing separately: have `ai/pipeline.py` write these fields itself
at process time (`ai/manifest.py` already computes most of it and is dead code —
`build_manifest()` is never called). Then `sha_confidence` becomes `recorded`.

## Build · 2 · Scoring and API

**4a. Fix the loader first — nothing else matters until it's done.**
`ai/eval/predictions.py` `load_predictions()` drops every strike because it
matches `_STRIKE_RE` against `description`, now always NULL. Replace that branch
with one driven by `action` + `fighter_id`:

- family/target from `PIPELINE_ACTION_MAP` in `ai/eval/schema.py` — verified to
  cover all 11 actions fight 62 emits, so no new mapping is needed;
- corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`, the rule
  `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts` `attributedCorner` already uses;
- keep the `description` regex only as a fallback for pre-migration rows.

**4b. Cross-fight scoring is almost free — `score.py` already supports it.**
`score(labels: FightLabels, preds: Predictions, tolerance_secs, strict_fighter)`
(`ai/eval/score.py:342`) takes the two sides as independent objects, and
`build_labels(video)` (`labels_db.py:69`) and `load_predictions(video)` each
resolve their own fight. So the pair is literally:

```python
score(build_labels("BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4"),
      load_predictions("BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4"))
```

The only work is in `cli.py`: accept `--reference` / `--run` (fight id or video),
resolve them through `pipeline_runs`, and add `--persist` to write the report
back into that row. `Report.video` is taken from the labels side, so the report
needs a second field naming the run — otherwise two runs' reports look identical.

**4c. Resolve corner to a person before comparing it.** The reference fight's
`corner` is a track slot; flip it inside that fight's `corner_swap` spans — at
read time only, never by mutating rows — then compare to the run's resolved
`fighter_id`. This is what turns read-back into real attribution accuracy
(see above). `frontend/src/utils/cornerSwap.ts` `isFrameSwapped` is the
equivalent rule already in the frontend.

**4d. Guard rails before any number is emitted.** Assert the pair really is one
bout: same `fps`, same `reported_frames`, same red/blue fighter ids, reference
has `labeled_at IS NOT NULL`, run has `purpose='ai_labeled'`. `score()` today
only *prints a warning* on an fps mismatch and carries on — across two uploads
that must become a refusal, because every frame index would be silently wrong.
Return an explicit *unmeasurable* result — never zeros — when a sub-metric has no
population: fight state today (0 `state` rows anywhere), and any sanity check
that ran on n = 0.

**4e. API.** New `eval_router` registered in `backend/app/main.py` with
`prefix="/eval"`, following `backend/app/api/routes/fights.py` conventions
(module-level `router`, `response_model`, Pydantic schemas beside the ORM model).
Live SQL for anything derived from `fight_events` / `fights` / `rounds`; the
stored `score_report` for accuracy. Sketch:

| Route | Serves |
|---|---|
| `GET /eval/labels/summary` | A · hero + tiles: per-family counts split by `purpose`, largest-fight share, activity by day |
| `GET /eval/labels/events` | B1/B2/B3 · counts by action × target × corner × state, filterable by fight and purpose |
| `GET /eval/fights` | C + D · ledger rows, span/coverage counts, open spans, seeded-vs-adjusted rounds, video-on-disk |
| `GET /eval/fights/{id}/coverage` | C4 · the coverage strip's lanes for one fight |
| `GET /eval/runs` | E · `pipeline_runs` joined to both fights, newest first |
| `GET /eval/runs/{id}/score` | E1–E9 · the stored `score_report` |
| `GET /eval/runs/{id}/sanity` | F1 · sanity report, each check carrying its population |
| `GET /eval/runs/{id}/corner` | F2 · corner accuracy — needs `--json` added to `ai/eval/corner_accuracy.py`, which prints only today |

**4f. Ordering.** 4a → 4c → 4b → insert the fight-62 row → 4d → persist a score
→ API → page. The first three steps alone turn today's F1 of 0 into ~45%.

## Build · 3 · Frontend — the `/lab` page

Conventions to follow (all verified): React 19 + TS + Vite, `react-router-dom`,
plain `fetch` with root-relative paths, **no chart library and no CSS framework**
— every visual is hand-written inline SVG plus inline `style={{}}` referencing
`var(--token)` from `frontend/src/index.css`.

### Wiring

- `frontend/src/App.tsx` — one `<Route path="/lab" element={<Lab />} />`.
- `frontend/src/components/Header.tsx:6` — add `{ label: 'Lab', to: '/lab' }` to
  `NAV_LINKS`.
- `frontend/vite.config.ts` — add an `/eval` proxy entry. **Put the API under
  `/eval/...`, not `/lab`**, so the client route and the API path never collide
  and the `Accept: text/html` bypass the `/fights` entry needs isn't repeated.
- New files: `frontend/src/pages/Lab.tsx` + `frontend/src/components/lab/*.tsx` +
  `frontend/src/hooks/useLab*.ts`, matching the existing one-folder-per-page rule.

### Tokens to add to `index.css`

None of these exist yet. Values come from the brief §14, which were checked with
the dataviz palette validator against the card surface including CVD simulation
(see `frontend-palette-collisions`):

```css
--status-good: #0ca30c;  --status-warning: #fab219;  --status-critical: #ef4444;
--status-unverified: #94a3b8;  --status-unmeasured: #64748b;
--state-striking: #0099b0;  --state-clinch: #e64a19;  --state-ground: #9085e9;
```

Do **not** reuse `AnnotationTimeline.tsx`'s STATE colours — its CLINCH `#ff7043`
and GROUND `#ff4d4d` are ΔE 6.6 apart and GROUND is the red corner.

### Reuse, don't rebuild

| Need | Reuse |
|---|---|
| B1 palette rows | `components/annotate/taxonomy.ts` `TOOL_GROUPS` — B1 is that list joined with counts; never hardcode the actions (the palette has `submission_attempt`, the brief says `submission`) |
| R\|B split, corner attribution | `utils/liveStats.ts` `attributedCorner` |
| B3 stacked bars | `components/player/SegBar.tsx` |
| E8 trend line | model on `components/player/PaceChart.tsx` (hand-rolled SVG, fixed `viewBox`, manual scale fns) |
| Stat tiles | `components/player/MiniStat.tsx`, `.inner-tile` |
| Card header + pills + view toggle | `components/annotate/AnnotationPanel.tsx` (incl. its `localStorage` view persistence) |
| Dense clickable rows | `components/player/LiveFeed.tsx` row anatomy |
| C4 coverage strip | **extract a shared mini-strip from `components/annotate/AnnotationTimeline.tsx`** — it already draws rounds / state / swap / excluded lanes and owns `SPAN_COLOR`; this is the highest-value refactor in the whole job |
| Purpose chips | `components/FightPurposeBadge.tsx`, `types/Fight.ts` `PURPOSE_COLORS` |

New primitives that genuinely don't exist: a sortable table with a sticky header
and expandable rows (there is **no `<table>` anywhere in the codebase**), a
heatmap cell, a dumbbell row, a dot strip, a column chart, and a `StatusBadge`
rendering all five states as **icon + text** (never colour alone).

### Prerequisite on two existing pages

`?frame=N` deep links are required by C4, E9 and G2. `grep -rn "useSearchParams"
src/` returns nothing — neither `pages/Player.tsx` nor `pages/Annotate.tsx` reads
a query param today. Add `useSearchParams` to both, seeking once on mount.

## Verification

1. `docker compose up -d db`, backend on `:8000`, `npm run dev` in `frontend/`.
2. **The scorer, first and on its own** — before any UI:
   `cd ai && ../.venv/bin/python -m eval.cli score --reference 60 --run 62 --json /tmp/r.json`
   must report a non-zero F1 near the ±12 f preview above (TP 84 / FP 63 / FN 143,
   F1 ≈ 45%). If it reports 0, blocker 1 is not fixed.
3. `eval.cli sanity fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4` must stop saying
   "0 in-round strikes" and must mark n = 0 checks `Not evaluated`.
4. Insert the fight-62 run row by hand (the agreed manual step) — see Build · 1 — then
   `curl localhost:8000/eval/runs` and confirm it lists exactly that run with
   `git_sha` `fc13725` and `constants_sha256` `b881cacf…` (verified: `constants.py`
   is unchanged between `fc13725` and the working tree, so this hash is right).
5. Open `/lab`. Check against the numbers in this plan: 800 training strikes,
   67% largest-fight share, elbow 0, 227 reference labels, 42.3% swap coverage,
   fight state `Not measured`, rounds `Seeded — not verified`.
6. Click a miss in E9 → lands on `/fights/60/annotate?frame=N` at that frame.
7. Re-run with a second `ai_labeled` upload to confirm the trend line and the
   run-to-run diff populate with two points rather than one.

## Still open

- **The Claude Design project was never readable.** After `/design-login`, import
  `Training Lab.html` and `assets/{brand.css,lab-accuracy.jsx,lab-app.jsx,
  lab-data.js,lab-parts.jsx,lab-sections.jsx}` and reconcile §5 against them —
  the design may have made layout decisions this plan should follow rather than
  re-derive.

/* ===== Training Lab — sections A · B · C · D ===== */

/* ---------- A · Overview ---------- */
function SectionA({ go }) {
  const h = L.hero,t = L.tiles;
  return <section className="lab-sec" id="sec-a">
    <div className="lab-grid-a">
      <div className="glass lab-card" style={{ padding: '20px 22px 18px', display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
        <div>
          <div className="label" style={{ marginBottom: 12 }}>Training set progress</div>
          <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'baseline', gap: 9, marginBottom: 3 }}>
            <span className="font-display" style={{ fontSize: 64, lineHeight: 0.86, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>{h.have}</span>
            <span className="font-display" style={{ fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 1, color: 'var(--text-disabled)' }}>/ {h.target}</span>
            <span style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 700, letterSpacing:0, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>strikes</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div>
          <HeroMeter have={h.have} target={h.target} ticks={[h.tick, h.target]} />
          <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 6, flexWrap: 'wrap', marginTop: 8, fontSize: 11.5, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-tertiary)' }}>
            <span style={{ color: 'var(--cyan-400)' }}>{h.pct}%</span><span style={{ color: 'var(--text-disabled)' }}>·</span>
            <span>{h.togo} to go</span><span style={{ color: 'var(--text-disabled)' }}>·</span>
            <span>~{h.days} days at the last-14-day pace ({h.pace} strikes/day)</span>
          </div>
          <div style={{ marginTop: 9, paddingTop: 9, borderTop: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05)', fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 600, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>
            {h.minutes} min of labelled round time across {h.fights} fights · ticks at 50 (useful for evaluation) and 300 (training target)
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div className="lab-tiles">
        <StatTile label="Label events" value={t.labelEvents} sub={`+${t.added} in the last 14 days · includes state marks`} onClick={() => go('sec-b')} />
        <StatTile label="Fights" value="3" sub="2 finished · 1 in progress · 1 exported to git" onClick={() => go('sec-d')} />
        <StatTile label="Strike detection F1" value="Not scorable" st="none" sub="No evaluation fixture yet" onClick={() => go('sec-e')}
        info="F1 always travels with its ground-truth count, fixture count, tolerance and pipeline version. A labelled fight on the manual track has no predictions — that is “not scorable”, not 0%." />
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>;
}

/* ---------- B · Annotated events ---------- */
const MIN_EX = 25;
const ZONES_C = [['head', 'head', '#ff4d1c'], ['body', 'body', '#ffb199'], ['leg', 'leg', '#f5f5f4'], ['ns', 'non-specific', '#9a9892']];
const famOf = (e) => e.trains && !['state span', 'takedown'].includes(e.trains) ? e.trains.split(' · ')[0] : null;

function ZonePanel({ sel, onClear }) {
  const fams = L.families;
  const zmax = Math.max(...fams.map((f) => f.total));
  const shown = sel ? fams.filter((f) => f.name === sel) : fams;
  const scale = sel ? Math.max(...shown.map((f) => f.total)) : zmax;
  const totals = ZONES_C.map(([k, l, c]) => ({ k, l, c, v: shown.reduce((s, f) => s + (f[k] || 0), 0) }));
  const grand = totals.reduce((s, t) => s + t.v, 0);
  return <div className="inner-tile" style={{ padding: '15px 16px' }}>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, marginBottom: 4 }}>
      <div className="label" style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>Target zone{sel ? ' · ' + sel : ' · all families'}</div>
      {sel && <button type="button" className="btn-glass" style={{ padding: '4px 9px', fontSize: 11 }} onClick={onClear}>Clear</button>}
    </div>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'baseline', gap: 8, marginBottom: 14, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
      <span className="font-display" style={{ fontSize: 34, lineHeight: 1, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>{grand}</span>
      <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>labels{sel ? '' : ' · 107 specific · 106 non-specific'}</span>
    </div>
    {totals.map((t) => <div key={t.k} style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '78px minmax(0,1fr) 34px', gap: 9, alignItems: 'center', marginBottom: 8 }}>
      <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>{t.l}</span>
      <div style={{ height: 10, background: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.045)', borderRadius: 2 }}>
        <div style={{ height: '100%', width: t.v / scale * 100 + '%', minWidth: t.v ? 3 : 0, background: t.c, borderRadius: '2px 4px 4px 2px' }}></div>
      </div>
      <span style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 800, textAlign: 'right', color: t.v ? 'var(--text-primary)' : 'var(--text-disabled)', fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums' }}>{t.v || '—'}</span>
    </div>)}
    <div style={{ marginTop: 12, paddingTop: 11, borderTop: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05)', fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 1.55, fontWeight: 600, color: 'var(--text-muted)', textWrap: 'pretty' }}>
      {sel ? `Only the zones ${sel} can land in carry a count — the rest are not part of the taxonomy.` :
      'Click a strike row to filter this panel to one family. Only the target zones a family can actually land in are drawn. At ~300 strikes the first model will collapse target (and probably family) — the labels keep the distinction for later.'}
    </div>
  </div>;
}

function SectionB({ openDrawer }) {
  const [view, setView] = useState('Palette actions');
  const [sel, setSel] = useState(null);
  const strikeTotal = 213,otherTotal = 37;
  const groups = useMemo(() => {
    const m = new Map();
    L.events.forEach((e) => {if (!m.has(e.g)) m.set(e.g, []);m.get(e.g).push(e);});
    return [...m.entries()];
  }, []);
  const max = Math.max(...L.events.map((e) => e.n));

  const famRows = useMemo(() => {
    const m = new Map();
    L.events.forEach((e) => {
      if (!e.trains || e.trains === 'state span' || e.trains === 'takedown') return;
      const fam = e.trains.split(' · ')[0];
      const cur = m.get(fam) || { n: 0, r: 0, b: 0, st: e.st };
      cur.n += e.n;cur.r += e.r || 0;cur.b += e.b || 0;
      if (e.st === 'miss') cur.st = 'miss';
      m.set(fam, cur);
    });
    return ['jab', 'cross', 'hook', 'uppercut', 'elbow', 'knee', 'kick', 'punch'].map((f) => ({ name: f, ...m.get(f) }));
  }, []);

  const famMax = Math.max(...L.families.map((f) => f.total));

  return <section className="lab-sec" id="sec-b">
    <div className="glass lab-card">
      <CardHead letter="B" title="Annotated events" meta={`${strikeTotal} strikes · ${otherTotal} other events · all labelled fights`}>
        <Pills opts={['Palette actions', 'Training classes', 'By fight']} value={view} onChange={setView} small />
        <button type="button" className="icon-btn" title="Reference — how labels become training data" onClick={openDrawer}
        style={{ width: 34, height: 34 }}><Icon n="menu_book" size={17} /></button>
      </CardHead>

      <div className="lab-b-grid">
        <div style={{ minWidth: 0 }}>
          {view === 'Palette actions' && <ChartFrame title="Events by type"
          note="Click a strike row to filter the target-zone panel to that family. Hairline marks the per-class minimum (25). One hue — the row label carries identity."
          table={<MiniTable head={['Action', 'Count', 'R', 'B', 'Trains as', 'Status']}
          rows={L.events.map((e) => [e.name, e.n, e.r ?? '—', e.b ?? '—', e.trains || '—', L.ST_META[e.st].label])} />}>
            <div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
              <div style={{ minWidth: 640 }}>
                {groups.map(([g, rows]) => <div key={g} style={{ marginBottom: 12 }}>
                  <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, padding: '0 10px 5px' }}>
                    <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 800, letterSpacing:0, color: 'var(--text-tertiary)' }}>{g}</span>
                    {g === 'Strikes' && <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 600, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>⇧ = body</span>}
                    <span style={{ flex: 1, height: 1, background: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.05)' }}></span>
                  </div>
                  {rows.map((e) => {
                    const fam = famOf(e);
                    const on = fam && fam === sel;
                    return <div key={e.name} onClick={() => fam && setSel(on ? null : fam)}
                    style={{ cursor: fam ? 'pointer' : 'default', borderRadius: 8,
                      background: on ? 'rgba(255,77,28,0.09)' : 'transparent',
                      boxShadow: on ? 'inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-cyan)' : 'none',
                      opacity: sel && !on ? 0.42 : 1, transition: 'opacity .12s, background .12s' }}>
                      <BarRow label={e.name} n={e.n} max={max}

      </div>
      <div className="lab-tiles">
        <StatTile label="Label events" value={t.labelEvents} sub={`+${t.added} in the last 14 days · includes state marks`} onClick={() => go('sec-b')} />
        <StatTile label="Fights" value="3" sub="2 finished · 1 in progress · 1 exported to git" onClick={() => go('sec-d')} />

}

/* ---------- B · Annotated events ---------- */
const MIN_EX = 25;
const ZONES_C = [['head', 'head', '#ff4d1c'], ['body', 'body', '#ffb199'], ['leg', 'leg', '#f5f5f4'], ['ns', 'non-specific', '#9a9892']];
const famOf = (e) => e.trains && !['state span', 'takedown'].includes(e.trains) ? e.trains.split(' · ')[0] : null;

function ZonePanel({ sel, onClear }) {
  const fams = L.families;
  const zmax = Math.max(...fams.map((f) => f.total));
  const shown = sel ? fams.filter((f) => f.name === sel) : fams;
  const scale = sel ? Math.max(...shown.map((f) => f.total)) : zmax;
  const totals = ZONES_C.map(([k, l, c]) => ({ k, l, c, v: shown.reduce((s, f) => s + (f[k] || 0), 0) }));
  const grand = totals.reduce((s, t) => s + t.v, 0);
  return <div className="inner-tile" style={{ padding: '15px 16px' }}>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, marginBottom: 4 }}>
      <div className="label" style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>Target zone{sel ? ' · ' + sel : ' · all families'}</div>

    </div>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'baseline', gap: 8, marginBottom: 14, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
      <span className="font-display" style={{ fontSize: 34, lineHeight: 1, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>{grand}</span>
      <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>labels{sel ? '' : ' · 107 specific · 106 non-specific'}</span>
    </div>
    {totals.map((t) => <div key={t.k} style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '78px minmax(0,1fr) 34px', gap: 9, alignItems: 'center', marginBottom: 8 }}>
      <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>{t.l}</span>
      <div style={{ height: 10, background: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.045)', borderRadius: 2 }}>
        <div style={{ height: '100%', width: t.v / scale * 100 + '%', minWidth: t.v ? 3 : 0, background: t.c, borderRadius: '2px 4px 4px 2px' }}></div>
      </div>
      <span style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 800, textAlign: 'right', color: t.v ? 'var(--text-primary)' : 'var(--text-disabled)', fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums' }}>{t.v || '—'}</span>
    </div>)}
    <div style={{ marginTop: 12, paddingTop: 11, borderTop: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05)', fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 1.55, fontWeight: 600, color: 'var(--text-muted)', textWrap: 'pretty' }}>
      {sel ? `Only the zones ${sel} can land in carry a count — the rest are not part of the taxonomy.` :
      'Click a strike row to filter this panel to one family. Only the target zones a family can actually land in are drawn. At ~300 strikes the first model will collapse target (and probably family) — the labels keep the distinction for later.'}
    </div>
  </div>;
}

function SectionB({ openDrawer }) {

    return [...m.entries()];
  }, []);
  const max = Math.max(...L.events.map((e) => e.n));

  const famRows = useMemo(() => {
    const m = new Map();
    L.events.forEach((e) => {
      if (!e.trains || e.trains === 'state span' || e.trains === 'takedown') return;

      const cur = m.get(fam) || { n: 0, r: 0, b: 0, st: e.st };
      cur.n += e.n;cur.r += e.r || 0;cur.b += e.b || 0;
      if (e.st === 'miss') cur.st = 'miss';
      m.set(fam, cur);
    });
    return ['jab', 'cross', 'hook', 'uppercut', 'elbow', 'knee', 'kick', 'punch'].map((f) => ({ name: f, ...m.get(f) }));
  }, []);

  const famMax = Math.max(...L.families.map((f) => f.total));

  return <section className="lab-sec" id="sec-b">

          rows={L.events.map((e) => [e.name, e.n, e.r ?? '—', e.b ?? '—', e.trains || '—', L.ST_META[e.st].label])} />}>
            <div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
              <div style={{ minWidth: 640 }}>
                {groups.map(([g, rows]) => <div key={g} style={{ marginBottom: 12 }}>

                    <span style={{ flex: 1, height: 1, background: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.05)' }}></span>
                  </div>
                  {rows.map((e) => {

                      <BarRow label={e.name} n={e.n} max={max}

          {view === 'Training classes' && <ChartFrame title="Training classes — export families"
          note="Collapsed to the eight export families. Rows under the 25-example minimum carry a Low chip."
          table={<MiniTable head={['Family', 'Count', 'R', 'B', 'Status']} rows={famRows.map((f) => [f.name, f.n, f.r, f.b, L.ST_META[f.st].label])} />}>
            {famRows.map((f) => <div key={f.name} onClick={() => setSel(sel === f.name ? null : f.name)}
            style={{ cursor: 'pointer', borderRadius: 8, background: sel === f.name ? 'rgba(255,77,28,0.09)' : 'transparent',
              boxShadow: sel === f.name ? 'inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-cyan)' : 'none',
              opacity: sel && sel !== f.name ? 0.42 : 1, transition: 'opacity .12s, background .12s' }}>
              <BarRow label={f.name} n={f.n} max={Math.max(...famRows.map((x) => x.n))}

            </div>)}
          </ChartFrame>}

          {view === 'By fight' && <ChartFrame title="By fight — small multiples, shared x-scale"
          note="Shared scale across all three panels: DRAGOJEVIC vs HONDA dominates every comparison.">
            <div className="lab-multiples">
              {L.byFight.map((f) => {
                const gmax = Math.max(...L.byFight.flatMap((x) => x.rows.map((r) => r[1])));
                return <div key={f.fight} className="inner-tile" style={{ padding: '12px 13px' }}>
                  <div style={{ fontSize: 11.5, fontWeight: 800, color: 'var(--text-secondary)', marginBottom: 9,
                    overflow: 'hidden', textOverflow: 'ellipsis', whiteSpace: 'nowrap' }}>{f.fight}</div>
                  {f.rows.map(([name, n]) => <div key={name} style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '1fr 40px', gap: 8, alignItems: 'center', marginBottom: 5 }}>

                      <div style={{ height: 7, background: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.04)', borderRadius: 2 }}>

                    </div>
                    <span style={{ fontSize: 11.5, fontWeight: 800, textAlign: 'right', fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums', color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>{n}</span>
                  </div>)}

              })}

          </ChartFrame>}
        </div>

        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 18, minWidth: 0 }}>
          <ZonePanel sel={sel} onClear={() => setSel(null)} />

          {/* B3 stacked */}
          <ChartFrame title="Strikes by fight state"
          table={<MiniTable head={['Family', 'STRIKING', 'CLINCH', 'GROUND', 'no state']}
          rows={L.stateMix.rows.map((r) => [r.name, r.STRIKING, r.CLINCH, r.GROUND, r.NONE])} />}>
            <div style={{ marginBottom: 11 }}>
              <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '62px 1fr', gap: 9, alignItems: 'center', marginBottom: 8 }}>
                <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 800, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>Overall</span>
                <StackedBar height={16} segs={[
                { name: 'STRIKING', v: L.stateMix.overall.STRIKING, c: L.STATE_C.STRIKING },
                { name: 'CLINCH', v: L.stateMix.overall.CLINCH, c: L.STATE_C.CLINCH },
                { name: 'GROUND', v: L.stateMix.overall.GROUND, c: L.STATE_C.GROUND },

}

/* ---------- D · Fights — ledger, spans & coverage ---------- */

    const r = [...L.ledger];
    if (sort === 'Strikes') r.sort((x, y) => (y.strikes || 0) - (x.strikes || 0));

    return r;
  }, [sort]);
  return <section className="lab-sec" id="sec-d">
    <div className="glass lab-card" data-comment-anchor="38e511ecb1-div-335-5">
      <CardHead title="Fights" meta="5 fights · 3 labelled on the manual track · 2 AI-processed · expand a fight for its spans and coverage">

        <Pills opts={SORTS} value={sort} onChange={setSort} small />
      </CardHead>
      <div className="lab-llist" data-comment-anchor="ed1c261f11-table-303-9">

                <div style={{ minWidth: 0 }}>
                  <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
                    <span style={{ fontSize: 13.5, fontWeight: 800, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>{f.fight}</span>
                    <Chip tone={f.track === 'AI' ? 'rgba(255,77,28,0.12)' : 'rgba(255,255,255,0.055)'}>{f.track}</Chip>
                    {f.role === 'Unlabelled' ?
                    <span style={{ fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>Unlabelled</span> :
                    <Chip tone="rgba(245,245,244,0.10)">{f.role}</Chip>}
                    {f.warn > 0 && <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 4, padding: '2px 7px', borderRadius: 6,
                      background: 'rgba(255,177,153,0.14)', border: '1px solid rgba(255,177,153,0.3)', color: '#ffb199', fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 800 }}>
                      <Icon n="warning" size={12} />{f.warn}</span>}

                onClick={() => {try {navigator.clipboard.writeText(`python -m eval.cli score fight_videos/${f.fight.toLowerCase().replace(/ vs /, '_').replace(/[^a-z_]/g, '')}.mp4 --json`);} catch (err) {}}}>

                <span style={{ fontWeight: 700, color: f.perMinWarn ? '#ffb199' : 'var(--text-muted)' }}>{f.perMin}/min</span>

function LM({ k, children }) {

27	  g.items

29	    .map((it) => ({ action: it.action, name: it.name, group: g.group, key: (it.num ?? it.key).toUpperCase() })),

40	 * what Annotate's own palette derives the moment a tool is first pressed
41	 * (`logTool()` in Annotate.tsx): a `fixedTarget` class always takes its own
42	 * fixed target, a `hasTarget` class keeps whatever head/body target the
43	 * event already had (defaulting to head), everything else has no target.
44	 * `success` is always `successForAction(newAction)`, same as a fresh label —
45	 * this is what keeps e.g. a retyped `takedown_landed` from silently ending
46	 * up with `success=null`, which nothing else in the app ever produces.

48	export function reclassifyPayload(
49	  newAction: string,

## Done — Training Lab (`/accuracy`) built out from the design

You were right that the real implementation had almost nothing compared to `Training Lab.html` — it only covered Section E ("Pipeline accuracy," per a documented scope-cut in `~/.claude/plans/i-have-now-reference-radiant-salamander.md`). I found and read that plan plus its more ambitious predecessor (`…-zippy-rabbit.md`), which had already worked out exactly what's honestly measurable with this app's real data — I built against that rather than re-deriving it, and re-verified the numbers against the live DB (5 training fights, 876 real label events, real corner-swap/state-mark data) before writing anything.

**New, built from real data — no fabrication:**
- **Section A (Overview)** — real training-strike count vs. the 300 target, labelled minutes, 14-day pace, and (per the `zippy-rabbit` finding, re-verified as still true) largest-fight dominance and per-family counts below the 25-example minimum, instead of the design's stale "days to go" framing
- **Section B (Annotated events)** — Palette actions / Training classes / By-fight views with real counts and R/B splits (reusing `TOOL_GROUPS`/`TRAINING_CLASSES`), a click-to-filter target-zone panel, and a strikes-by-fight-state stacked bar derived the same way `AnnotationTimeline` derives state segments
- **Section D (Fights ledger)** — every real fight, expandable to a coverage strip (rounds/state/swaps/excluded/density) plus real provenance (labeller, segmentation source via the real `segmentation_needs_review` field) and honest per-fight warnings
- **Section F** — reproduced verbatim as the design's own "TODO — still open" placeholder, since the designer never finished it either
- **Section E** — your existing, already-solid implementation, reskinned into the new card/typography system with the last hardcoded cyan hex cleaned up

**New files:** `hooks/useLabelledEvents.ts`, `hooks/useFightLedger.ts`, `components/accuracy/{LabOverview,AnnotatedEvents,FightLedger,CoverageStrip,SectionIndex,PipelineHealthTodo}.tsx`, plus a `FAMILY_BY_ACTION` addition to `trainingDataTaxonomy.ts`.

**Explicitly left out** (matching the design's own admission or genuine infra gaps): the reference drawer, corner-check accuracy (no backend endpoint exists), and per-event keypoint confidence.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` succeeds, eslint clean (remaining `set-state-in-effect` warnings are a pre-existing repo-wide pattern, not something I introduced), and I smoke-tested every new query shape directly against your running backend — all real, non-empty data. Same caveat as the last two pages: no browser tool here, so I couldn't screenshot it — worth a look at `:5173/accuracy` before calling it done.
